pos.personaBrief: The Times 1931 describes luring opponents into a false sense of security then transforming defence into attack; Chapman's own view credits chances from being driven back and breaking swiftly. Counter-attack over possession.

pro.personaBrief: Buchan's plan aimed at a goal from three or four touches out of defence and the system was built on quick, incisive counters, though a deep half-back took short passes from the stopper.

est.personaBrief: The WM gave set roles (stopper, full-backs, half-backs) and a drilled plan, but wingers played inside and James dropped deep, while the centre-forward stayed central.

lar.personaBrief: Bastin stood ten yards in from the touchline and, with Hulme, scored 53 goals in 1932-33; wingers were finishers from inside positions and an extra man was kept in midfield.

blo.personaBrief: Defence in depth with a stopper guarding the penalty-box edge; no source describes pressing, and the team retreated and then countered.

mar.personaBrief: Conflicting evidence: Buchan's 1925 centre-half guarded an area, but Roberts as stopper blotted out the centre-forward, full-backs took wingers and half-backs inside-forwards, so mostly man-oriented.

pla.personaBrief: Chapman imposed one system and told players 'never mind what the other team does, this is what you are going to do'; away form relied on the counter model.

res.personaBrief: Chapman was the first manager to organise the winning of matches methodically; he allowed spectacle only when two goals up and accepted a worse home record for results.

sis.personaBrief: The Times 1931 says players sank their individuality in the team; Roberts did what he was told, and players were fitted to roles ('horses for courses').

jog.personaBrief: Roles were matched to types: powerful Hapgood, old-fashioned stopper Roberts, but also James's slide-rule passing as a creative playmaker and a deep half-back who passes.

bas.personaBrief: Arsenal were the Bank of England club, building by purchase with no academy players; Chapman wanted team men worth their price and disliked disturbance from changes.

lid.personaBrief: Chapman would never tolerate slackness and was a disciplinarian, yet encouraged players to voice opposition to ideas and held weekly meetings.
